extracted.intended_audience: YouTube creators, viewers, and anyone seeking to understand how YouTube Trending Charts are generated
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and signals YouTube uses to determine which videos appear on Trending Charts (category-specific, country-level lists of popular videos). Covers aims, signals, content/safety filters, and visibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to chart topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Are relevant to the topic of the chart
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts vary by category (e.g., Trending Movie Trailers, Trending Music Videos, Trending Gaming Videos) and a video should be topical to the specific chart to be surfaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid growth (velocity / 'temperature')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube considers how quickly the video’s view count (or 'temperature') is growing as a signal. Trending Charts are updated roughly every 30 minutes, so rapid recent growth matters for placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not misleading / clickbaity / sensational
rubrics_metrics.description: Are not misleading, clickbaity, or sensational
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts aim to avoid surfacing videos that are misleading or sensational. This is an explicit aim in selecting trending videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showcase a diversity of creators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts aim to balance creator diversity alongside other considerations when deciding which videos to surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: View count
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw view count is one of the signals considered when producing charts, but it is combined with other signals, so the highest view count doesn't necessarily equal #1. Note: views from YouTube ads are excluded when measuring for trending charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where views are coming from
rubrics_metrics.description: Where views are coming from, including outside of YouTube
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traffic source (on-platform and off-platform) is considered as a signal for chart ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic of the video
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the video's subject matter matches the chart/category is considered (overlaps with relevance to chart topic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age of the video
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How recently the video was uploaded is used as a signal; trending charts surface popular new videos rather than older evergreen views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative performance versus recent uploads from the same channel
rubrics_metrics.description: How the video performs compared to other recent uploads from the same channel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts consider a video's performance relative to the channel's recent baseline to identify outsized performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and content-appropriateness filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Filters to avoid excessive profanity, mature content, violence, or otherwise inappropriate material
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube applies safety filters so that videos containing excessive profanity, mature content, violence, or disparaging content are less likely to appear on Trending Charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-personalized / country-level uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Trending Charts aren’t personalized and display the same trending videos to all viewers in the same country
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because charts are not personalized, users may see videos in Charts that are in languages different from their browser settings; charts are uniform within a country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update frequency and ranking dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Charts are updated roughly every 30 minutes; videos may move up, move down, or stay the same with each update
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent updates mean rankings are dynamic and reflect recent changes in signals; combining multiple signals means the video with the highest daily view count may not be #1 at a given update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of ad-generated views
rubrics_metrics.description: Views from YouTube ads are not included in a video’s view count when measuring videos for trending charts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid ad views do not contribute to trending measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No paid placement or favoritism
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube doesn't accept payment for placement on trending charts and doesn't favor specific creators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trending placement is independent of payment; YouTube states it does not favor particular creators for chart inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and Restricted Mode visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A video can only appear on Charts if its privacy setting is public; certain videos may be hidden if Restricted Mode is turned on
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only publicly visible videos are eligible for charts; users with Restricted Mode enabled may not see some trending videos.
